CONTRACT v3: only `title` (≤6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (≤140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/lead/body/chips/cards). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form; a footnote's source_url may render as a small domain chip, never as a naked URL in body copy. Never render: held corridors, Gulf counterparties, authority contacts, internal dock-status fields. DC SPECIFICS: hub gates banned terms respected on all renderables (no federal-zone citation or related vocabulary, no 'NPS permit'/'NPS concession' phrasing, no dock-status vocabulary); the speed-rule section is DC's headline asset — the District's own harbor code (19 DCMR § 1027) names hydrofoils, states its purpose in wash/wake terms, exempts hydrofoils under Mayoral demonstration permits (§ 1027.3), and vests limit-setting in the Mayor (§ 1027.1) — presented factually and calmly; base times respect posted limits everywhere. Bodies with unverified posture (Prince George's County) or not deep-profiled (DOEE, USACE) are omitted, as are the hub's 2019-shutdown daily-ridership figure and congestion-rank chip (unverified per research). Private landing controllers are not authorities and do not appear.

copy.framing: Two ways to partner — a genuine choice. Washington's landscape leans Enable: no public agency operates water transit in the region today, and the landing map runs through permits and agreements rather than procurement.
copy.enable_track: Grant landing access at existing marinas and piers and a permitting pathway for a pilot corridor. Private capital finances the fleet; privately committed employer demand fills the seats. The ask is access, not money.
copy.operate_track: The region's transit agencies procure service today and have studied Potomac commuter ferries. Navier vessels can be procured the way transit vehicles are procured — if and when an authority chooses to run a public water network.

copy.headline: Your code already contemplates hydrofoils.
copy.framing: The District's harbor rules cap vessel speed at 6 mph on the Washington Channel, the upper Potomac, and the Anacostia — and state their purpose in wash and wake terms. A foiling, electric Navier satisfies that purpose inherently.
copy.ask: The mechanism already exists: District regulations exempt hydrofoils operated for demonstration under a permit issued by the Mayor, and give the Mayor standing authority to set vessel speed limits. Our ask: measure us, then use the code as written.

expander.title: What speed-rule relief unlocks
body: District regulation caps vessel speed at 6 mph in the Washington Channel, on the Potomac above Arlington Memorial Bridge, and on the Anacostia, with a 10 mph band along the Old Town waterfront. The rule states its own purpose: speed must be regulated to avoid harm from "the effect of the wash or wake the vessels raise."

The same regulation already names hydrofoils — and already contains relief. Its speed limits do not apply to hydrofoils operated for demonstration or experimentation purposes under a permit issued by the Mayor, and the Mayor holds standing authority to set vessel speed limits.

Our ask: measure wake and noise foilborne, grant a demonstration permit for a defined corridor, and set foil-specific limits where the measured record shows the rule's purpose is served. To be plain: a demonstration permit covers demonstration operation — scheduled service would rely on the Mayor's standing limit-setting authority.
Precedent: Stockholm's public transport authority runs an electric hydrofoil ferry at roughly twice the posted zone speed under a low-wake exemption.

rule_basis.detail: Mayor authorized to establish vessel speed limits for District waters
outcome-based wash/wake duty — quoted verbatim in expander
speed limits do not apply to hydrofoil or air cushion vessels operated for demonstration or experimentation purposes under a Mayoral permit

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: Zero-emission. Near-silent. Almost no wake.
copy.subline: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels — the traits that matter for harbor rules and river neighbors are built into the hull, not bolted on.
copy.body: The N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots, lifted clear of the water for a smooth, wake-free ride. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

reference.title: Reference

copy.intro: Washington's water-transportation landscape spans federal, District, regional, and municipal bodies. We seek conversations — nothing here implies approval, endorsement, or commitment by any body named.

bodies.body: National Park Service — George Washington Memorial Parkway
bodies.role: Administers the Virginia-side Potomac parkland, including the working marinas at Columbia Island and Daingerfield Island; docking as approved by the Superintendent.

bodies.body: National Park Service — National Capital Parks-East & Piscataway Park
bodies.role: Administers the working marinas at James Creek and Fort Washington — with the Parkway, steward of four of the network's eleven landings.
Designated Marine Highway M-495 across the Anacostia, Occoquan, and Potomac — a route whose designation includes passenger ferry services.
District transportation department; leads the 30-year Anacostia Waterfront Initiative transportation program. Plans and permits; operates no vessels.
Holds standing authority under District harbor rules to set vessel speed limits and to permit hydrofoil demonstration operation.

bodies.body: MPD Harbor Patrol / DC Harbor Master
bodies.role: Patrols all District waterways, administers vessel registration and marine event permits, and enforces the harbor rules, including speed limits.

bodies.body: DMPED (Deputy Mayor for Planning & Economic Development)
bodies.role: Built and funded the Diamond Teague piers — the District's own commercial water-transit landing at Navy Yard.

bodies.body: US Coast Guard — Captain of the Port, Maryland–National Capital Region
bodies.role: Federal navigation-safety authority for the Potomac and Anacostia; a standing stakeholder for any scheduled service.
Owns and operates the Alexandria City Marina — the network's primary interchange landing; its waterfront plan embraces water taxis among core travel modes.
Commuter transit agency for the I-95 corridor; has repeatedly studied Potomac commuter ferry service from Woodbridge. Study-stage — nothing procured.
Regional planning and convening bodies; produced the commuter-ferry feasibility groundwork on travel times, docking locations, and environmental screening.
Water-rule authorities for the Maryland and Virginia reaches of the southern corridors.
